title: In Seoul, a Conversation About Research That Keeps Listening
summary: Park's summer research visit put lasting relationships with older adults at the center of AI and robotics design.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post

paragraphs.text: Chorong Park brought a relationship-centered view of technology research to a summer visit at Seoul National University. Hosted by Hyunggu Jung's lab in the College of Nursing, she shared recent work on aging, AI, and companion robots.

In her August 19, 2026, reflection, Park emphasized what happens beyond recruitment: returning, listening, offering support, and involving older adults in design over time. She described that sustained engagement as central to building trust.

The discussion also challenged technoageism, including the tendency to treat older adults as passive users or people to be monitored. Park instead emphasized their role in shaping technologies that respect privacy, autonomy, dignity, and joy.
The visit included exchanges with researchers from Taiwan and a follow-up conversation with Yung-Ju Chang of National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University about possible future collaboration.

The research lesson Park highlighted travels across settings: participation is not a box to check once. It is an ongoing relationship that can change the questions a team asks and whose perspective guides the work.
